recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what the members have in common and how you would write it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Read the property the members share
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both halves of the property are needed: the set the members are drawn from, and the two bounds.
lines: Every member of A is an integer, and the members run from −3 up to 3 with none missing.
So the property shared by the members is: x ∈ Z and −3 ≤ x ≤ 3.

recall.must_convey: That every member is an integer lying between −3 and 3, both ends included.
accept: all the members are integers from minus three to three
the property is x is an integer and minus three is less than or equal to x less than or equal to three
they are the integers with absolute value at most three
anni integers, minus three nunchi three varaku
say the common property of the members

steps.why: Set-builder form replaces the list by one property, so the property has to pick out these seven members and nothing else. Naming the set of integers is half of that, and the bounds are the other half.
common_mistakes: Saying only that the members run from −3 to 3 and leaving out that they are integers.
Reading the list as the natural numbers, which drops the negative members and 0.
steps.memory_tip: Ask two questions of the list: what kind of number is every member, and where does the list start and stop.

steps.label: Write the set-builder form
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The colon is read as the words 'such that'. Keep both conditions inside the braces.
lines: Set-builder form writes a set as {x : the property x satisfies}.
Here the property has two parts, x ∈ Z and −3 ≤ x ≤ 3.

recall.must_convey: That A is written as {x : x ∈ Z, −3 ≤ x ≤ 3}.
accept: A is the set of all x such that x is an integer and minus three is less than or equal to x less than or equal to three
write it as x colon x belongs to Z comma minus three to three
the set of all integers x with modulus x at most three
set builder form lo x belongs to Z ani rasi bounds cheppali
A equals set of x such that x is an integer between minus three and three inclusive
heard_as: set of all x such that

steps.why: Both conditions must stay inside the braces, because either one alone describes a different set: x ∈ Z alone gives every integer, and the bounds alone give every number between −3 and 3.
common_mistakes: Writing A = {x : −3 ≤ x ≤ 3} without x ∈ Z, which then includes fractions such as 1/2.
Using strict inequalities, A = {x : x ∈ Z, −3 < x < 3}, which drops −3 and 3.
Writing A = {x : x ∈ N, −3 ≤ x ≤ 3}, which has no negative members.
steps.memory_tip: Read the braces aloud: 'the set of all x such that ...'. If the sentence does not name a kind of number, a condition is missing.
